cf.title: CAST(... ON DEFAULT) - WIP build on top of Error-Safe User Functions

input.subject: CAST(... ON DEFAULT) - WIP build on top of Error-Safe User Functions

verdict_reasoning: The goal has support: the syntax is in the SQL standard and a committer committed the prerequisite patches. The design is not yet agreed. Reviewers and the author still disagree on which errors fall back to DEFAULT for nested and constant-folded casts (standards-compat-1). No committer has accepted ERROR { SAFE | UNSAFE }, which keeps two of the three concerns raised against CREATE CAST ... WITH SAFE FUNCTION (standards-compat-2).

brief.title: Add CAST(... DEFAULT expr ON CONVERSION ERROR) syntax
brief.problem: A failed type cast aborts the whole query, so users cannot fall back to a value when one input does not convert. The thread points to bulk ETL from all-text tables and to existing TRY_CAST in SQL Server and the Oracle CAST clause. The syntax was accepted into the SQL standard after SQL:2023.
brief.proposed_design: The parser builds a new SafeTypeCastExpr that evaluates only the conversion with an ErrorSaveContext and evaluates the DEFAULT expression only when that conversion fails softly. A new pg_proc.proerrorsafe flag marks functions that can report soft errors, and a cast is accepted only if its function is marked. The planner folds constants under a soft-error context, with a WIP patch to avoid evaluating DEFAULT when the cast succeeds.
user_visible_surface: SQL syntax: CAST(expr AS type DEFAULT expr ON CONVERSION ERROR) and CAST(expr AS type ERROR ON CONVERSION ERROR).
CREATE FUNCTION and ALTER FUNCTION option ERROR { UNSAFE | SAFE }.
New catalog column pg_proc.proerrorsafe, set true for built-in cast and input functions.
New error at parse time when the cast function is not error safe, for example in citext casts.
fmgr README: any function call in an expression compiled with an ErrorSaveContext may receive one.
author_claims: Almost all built-in pg_cast functions are now error safe; many type patches were committed in March 2026.
Making only part of an expression tree error safe is not feasible, so some nested cases behave differently.
Not all functions are error safe, so CAST ... DEFAULT cannot be fully consistent in every case.
The DEFAULT expression is evaluated normally and can raise its own error.
proerrorsafe puts no load on the executor, according to Corey Huinker.
brief.thread_state: Peter Eisentraut committed many prerequisite patches, rejected CREATE CAST ... WITH SAFE FUNCTION and suggested a pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() function instead; the patch then moved to PG20 CommitFests. Corey Huinker and Henson Choi still disagree with the author on nested casts, constant folding order and reg* lookup failures, and v35 adds two LLM-generated WIP patches.
unclear: No committer has said whether ERROR { SAFE | UNSAFE } on CREATE FUNCTION is acceptable.
The material does not say whether SQL and PL/pgSQL functions may be marked ERROR SAFE without any check.
The material does not settle whether a missing schema or relation in a reg* cast should fall back to DEFAULT.
No performance numbers are given for the new safe function-call steps or the soft-error constant folding.
The intended rule for nested casts and ARRAY[] arguments, evaluated before or after the outer cast, is still disputed.

objections.title: Error-catching rules depend on constant folding, plan shape and nesting
objections.failure_scenario: An ETL script tests `cast(cast('a' as int) as text default null on conversion error)` with literals and gets an error, but the same query over a column returns NULL. A prepared statement may fold the cast in a custom plan but not in a generic plan. The user finds out in production, when the same data gives a different result.
objections.argument: Message #75 shows two nested casts with the same value that differ only in whether the literal is typed: one returns NULL, the other errors. Messages #99 and #100 disagree on whether evaluation is top-down or bottom-up, and #99 adds an ARRAY-only flag, `arg_errorsafe`. The proposal does not tie these rules to the standard text. Once released, whatever v35 does becomes the behaviour users depend on.
objections.author_must_show: Which errors fall back to DEFAULT, stated once as a rule tied to the standard text, and does that rule give the same result for literals, columns, parameters and nested casts?

critic.reasoning: Message #75 shows two nested casts of the same value with different results, and messages #99 and #100 still disagree on evaluation order. The author's summary in message #94 calls the inconsistency unsolvable and states no single rule.

objections.title: ERROR SAFE function option repeats the churn that CREATE CAST SAFE drew
objections.failure_scenario: An extension makes its cast and input functions use ereturn(), but it does not ship a new version script with `alter function ... error safe`. `cast(x as citext default ... on conversion error)` then fails at parse time on every row. The user finds out at the first run, and pg_input_is_valid() on the same type still works.
objections.argument: Message #70 rejected CREATE CAST ... WITH SAFE FUNCTION because it forces new extension SQL files, and because error-safe input functions got only a documentation note. Moving the marker to CREATE FUNCTION (#89, #94) answers the first point but not the second or third. #94 now also gates input-function coercion on proerrorsafe, so CAST DEFAULT and pg_input_is_valid() use different rules for the same input function. No committer has accepted the new syntax.
objections.author_must_show: Why is a catalog flag that every extension must set needed, when pg_input_is_valid() already relies on the documented ereturn() convention without one?

critic.reasoning: Message #88 argues that an unmarked design surprises users, and #96 calls the default false a protection. No committer has answered the input-function and extension-churn points from message #70, and #94 gates I/O coercion on a flag that pg_input_is_valid() does not use.

objections.title: Smaller first step suggested by the committer is not taken
objections.failure_scenario: The project commits new grammar, a catalog column, new CREATE FUNCTION syntax and executor opcodes in one step. Nested-cast semantics are still disputed, so each future answer to that dispute becomes a user-visible behavior change to standard syntax.
objections.argument: Message #70 proposes pg_cast_conversion_succeeds(srcvalue, desttype) as a first step, mirroring pg_input_is_valid(), so the higher-level syntax can wait. Message #81 proposes limiting the first version to casts that CoerceViaIO can handle. Messages #98 and #100 show the reviewer and the author still disagree on whether inner casts and constant-folded failures fall back. v35 still ships all of it together.
objections.author_must_show: Why not commit pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() or a CoerceViaIO-only subset first, and settle the nested-cast rules before fixing them in standard syntax?

critic.reasoning: Message #71 answers the staged step only by calling it IS CASTABLE, and #59 defers that to a separate patch. The committer kept reviewing the full patch (#76), so staging is a choice and no condition, but the nested-cast rules are still open.

objections.title: Syntax ships while its standard definition is still being amended
objections.failure_scenario: Postgres releases DEFAULT clauses that accept any expression, including aggregates, window functions and subqueries (message #99). If the standard amendment then restricts the DEFAULT operand, every query using the broader form becomes a Postgres-only dialect that cannot be narrowed without breaking users.
objections.argument: In messages #2 and #8, the risk named was that the committee would change the spelling, and the agreed plan was to wait for something solid. Message #84, in April 2026, still amends the paper: NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR is removed and the DEFAULT operand becomes an implicitly typed value specification. The patch dropped NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR (#85), but it does not say how the broad DEFAULT form matches the amended text.
objections.author_must_show: Does the amended standard text allow any value expression, including aggregates and subqueries, as the DEFAULT operand, and has that amendment been accepted?

critic.reasoning: In message #21 the standard's author called the aggregate restriction arbitrary, and a Postgres superset of the standard is no failure. But the thread does not say whether the amendment in message #84 was accepted, which was the condition set in message #8.

refuted.title: Error-safe marker keeps the costs of the rejected CREATE CAST SAFE design
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension such as citext has C cast functions that already use ereturn(). A user runs CAST(x AS citext DEFAULT NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR) and gets a parse-time error. The extension must then ship a new SQL script with ALTER FUNCTION ... ERROR SAFE, and users must run ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE before the standard feature works.
refuted.argument: In message #70 the committer rejected CREATE CAST ... WITH SAFE FUNCTION for three reasons: it is nonstandard syntax joining two standard features, type input functions got no such flag, and it forces churn in extensions. Moving the marker to pg_proc as ERROR { SAFE | UNSAFE } (messages #89, #94) answers only the first reason, and only in part, because CREATE FUNCTION syntax is still extended. The second and third reasons still apply, since unmarked functions are rejected at parse time. No committer has replied to the new design.
refuted.author_must_show: Why does a pg_proc flag answer the input-function precedent and the extension-churn concern from message #70, when pg_input_is_valid() needs no such flag?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2, which makes the same point and adds the mismatch with pg_input_is_valid().

refuted.title: Committer's smaller first step was set aside while the patch grew
refuted.failure_scenario: A committer who picks up v35 has to review four new executor opcodes, soft-error constant folding in clauses.c, a new ParseState field and two LLM-generated WIP patches together. Disputes on nested casts and folding order (messages #87, #99, #100) are still open, so whatever behaviour ships becomes a compatibility promise that later releases must keep.
refuted.argument: Message #70 proposed pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() as a first step, so users could build the fallback with CASE while the full feature matured. The thread did not take up this step. Since then the patch has added EEOP_FUNCEXPR_SAFE variants and error-safe evaluate_expr (message #97), and reviewers still disagree on the expected results (messages #99, #100).
refuted.author_must_show: What prevents committing pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() first, as proposed in message #70, and adding the DEFAULT syntax only after the nested-cast semantics are agreed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of maintenance-fit-4, which also covers the CoerceViaIO-only subset from message #81.

refuted.title: Standard text was still being amended in 2026
refuted.failure_scenario: Postgres ships DEFAULT accepting any expression, including aggregates and subqueries (message #99). A later standard text limits or changes what DEFAULT may hold. Users' queries then depend on behaviour that Postgres has to keep as a nonstandard superset, or change.
refuted.argument: The 2023 attempt was marked Rejected in message #9 because the committee had not settled the syntax (messages #2, #7, #8). The syntax was accepted later (message #14), but in message #84 the paper's author reports a draft bug fix that removes NULL ON CONVERSION ERROR and changes the DEFAULT clause. v29 removed the NULL form. The thread does not say whether the draft is final or how far v35 follows the new DEFAULT rule.
refuted.author_must_show: Has the amendment from message #84 been accepted, and does v35's DEFAULT clause match its final wording?

refuted.title: proerrorsafe brings back the extension upgrade churn rejected in message #70
refuted.failure_scenario: A user runs pg_upgrade on a cluster with hstore or a third-party type whose C cast functions are already soft-error capable. After the upgrade, proerrorsafe is false for those functions, so CAST ... DEFAULT fails at parse time. It keeps failing until the extension ships an update script with ALTER FUNCTION ... ERROR SAFE and the user runs ALTER EXTENSION UPDATE.
refuted.argument: Message #70 rejected CREATE CAST ... WITH SAFE FUNCTION partly because it would force new extension SQL files and forced upgrades, and noted that error-safe input functions needed no catalog marker. Moving the marker from pg_cast to pg_proc (message #94) keeps that cost, and every pg_dump and extension script must now carry the new attribute. Message #96 sees the default false as a protection, but the material does not weigh it against the upgrade cost that message #70 named. The patch also shows no way to mark contrib functions without an extension version bump.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a persistent pg_proc flag that every error-safe extension must set through an update script better than the no-marker approach used for soft-error input functions?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-2. The pg_upgrade case is the same extension update cost seen from another side.

refuted.title: No committer owns the patch since the prerequisite work landed
refuted.failure_scenario: After commit, a bug report arrives about a wrong fallback or a crash in the safe-cast path, for example in eval_const_expressions or a JIT step. The fix needs someone who knows the parser, the planner, the executor and the JIT all at once. No committer has reviewed the main patch, so the report waits.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest history shows Peter Eisentraut removed himself as committer on 2026-04-10, after committing the prerequisite patches (messages #70, #76). Since then the reviewers are non-committers, and message #101 adds two LLM-generated WIP patches that touch clauses.c and parse_collate.c. The main patch is about 160 KiB across the parser, planner, executor, JIT and ruleutils. Message #73 and message #75 show that design questions in this code are still being found through segfaults.
refuted.author_must_show: Which committer has agreed to review the v35 design across parser, planner and executor, and to own fixes after commit?

critic.reasoning: A committer commented on the main patch in message #70 and said in #76 he would keep reviewing it; he withdrew on the day the entry moved to PG20. Ownership belongs in the committability field and does not show a design flaw.

refuted.title: proerrorsafe is an unchecked promise that future changes can break silently
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds an ereport(ERROR) to a helper that a built-in cast function calls, such as a namespace lookup or numeric rounding. The function keeps proerrorsafe = true and no test fails. A user's ETL job that relies on DEFAULT ... ON CONVERSION ERROR then aborts on a bad row.
refuted.argument: Message #90 found this already: get_namespace_oid() raises a hard error under text_regclass, so a missing schema aborts while a missing relation falls back. Message #98 notes that SQL and PL/pgSQL functions can be declared ERROR SAFE with no check, and message #96 warns that the word "safe" overstates the guarantee. Peter's third objection to WITH SAFE FUNCTION in message #70 was the churn it forces on extensions. A per-function flag still requires new extension scripts that run ALTER FUNCTION, and pg_dump must carry the flag permanently.
refuted.author_must_show: What check or regression test fails when a function marked ERROR SAFE gains a hard-error path, and how is this different in cost for extensions from the CREATE CAST variant rejected in message #70?

critic.reasoning: An unchecked declaration copies IMMUTABLE and PARALLEL SAFE, as message #98 notes, and the documentation says errors not reported softly abort as usual. A missed hard-error path raises an error, which is loud; the extension-script point duplicates standards-compat-2.

refuted.title: Soft-error plumbing spreads into common parser and planner paths
refuted.failure_scenario: Every query passes through eval_const_expressions and coerce_to_target_type. With an ErrorSaveContext now threaded through evaluate_expr and ParseState, a planner or parser change in a later release can turn on soft-error handling by mistake. Extensions calling these APIs then see changed signatures or semantics.
refuted.argument: Message #97 adds p_escontext to ParseState, refactors every ece_evaluate_expr call, and adds four new function-call opcodes. Message #68 notes that fcinfo->context is a generic pointer that triggers also use. The fmgr README hunk widens the contract to every function call in an expression compiled with an ErrorSaveContext, including functions not marked ERROR SAFE. The thread gives no performance numbers for plain queries or for the new steps.
refuted.author_must_show: What measurements show no cost to queries without CAST ... DEFAULT, and which extension-visible functions change signature or fcinfo->context behavior?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is a future mistake by another patch, with no concrete regression. The design keeps a separate node and separate opcodes so plain casts are not burdened (messages #23, #55, #97), though measurements would still be a fair request.

refuted.title: Text-source fallback is already possible with pg_input_is_valid()
refuted.failure_scenario: An ETL user loading an all-text staging table can write `case when pg_input_is_valid(col, 'integer') then col::integer else -1 end` today. The patch adds new grammar, a SafeTypeCastExpr node, new executor opcodes and a pg_proc column. Message #81 names exactly this case as the main use.
refuted.argument: Since Postgres 16, pg_input_is_valid() tests the soft-error input path for any type, which covers text-to-type conversion through CoerceViaIO. The proposal still adds things it cannot do: function-based casts such as numeric to integer, which round differently from I/O (message #24), and standard syntax (message #14). Message #70 proposed a smaller pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() function first. The thread has no reply that weighs that staged path against the full syntax, so a committer would likely ask for that comparison.
refuted.author_must_show: Which real workloads need fallback on non-text, function-based casts that pg_input_is_valid() or a pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() function could not serve with modest effort?

critic.reasoning: pg_input_is_valid() cannot test function-based casts, which round differently from I/O conversion (message #24), as the objection itself says. The staged-path question is covered by maintenance-fit-4.

refuted.title: Demand shown is for text-source ETL, which pg_input_is_valid already covers
refuted.failure_scenario: An ETL user loads an all-text staging table and needs per-row fallback values. Today they can write case when pg_input_is_valid(t, 'int') then t::int else -1 end. If the patch goes in, every function author and every future cast patch must also keep pg_proc.proerrorsafe and soft-error paths correct, mostly for cases that no user in the thread asked for.
refuted.argument: The only concrete use case in the thread is mass ETL from all-text tables (message #81), and the brief names the same one. For text sources, conversion goes through input functions, and pg_input_is_valid already tests them softly. The proposal adds more than that: a new pg_proc column, ERROR { SAFE | UNSAFE } on CREATE and ALTER FUNCTION, and soft-error constant folding, which mainly serve non-text and user-defined casts. Message #70 suggested shipping a checking function first and building the full feature later, and no field report in the thread asks for more than that.
refuted.author_must_show: Which users need DEFAULT ON CONVERSION ERROR for non-text source casts or user-defined ERROR SAFE functions, where the pg_input_is_valid workaround is not enough?

critic.reasoning: The material shows lasting demand: the syntax is in the SQL standard, SQL Server and Oracle have equivalents, message #2 approves of the goal, and a committer committed the prerequisite patches. proerrorsafe defaults to false, so unmarked functions cost only users of the feature.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: New pg_proc.proerrorsafe column needs a catversion bump, and upgraded extension functions stay unmarked until an update script runs.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: Adds pg_proc.proerrorsafe and sets it in pg_proc.dat for built-in cast and input functions.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The fmgr README widens the ErrorSaveContext contract, and parse_coerce.h, optimizer.h and ParseState change.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: Adds standard CAST ... ON CONVERSION ERROR grammar and nonstandard ERROR { SAFE | UNSAFE } on CREATE and ALTER FUNCTION.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: clauses.c folds constants under a soft-error context, and a WIP patch changes when DEFAULT is evaluated.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump.c and ruleutils.c must emit the ERROR SAFE attribute and deparse the new cast form in views.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: New expression node, executor opcodes, JIT steps and a per-function flag that every cast function author must keep correct.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Touches execExpr.c, execExprInterp.c, llvmjit_expr.c and eval_const_expressions; the thread gives no measurements for plain queries.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: What single rule decides which errors fall back to DEFAULT, and does it give the same result for literals, columns, parameters and nested casts?
Why does CAST ... DEFAULT need a pg_proc flag that every extension must set, when pg_input_is_valid() relies on the ereturn() convention without one?
Has the standard amendment from message #84 been accepted, and does it allow aggregates and subqueries as the DEFAULT operand?
Why not commit pg_cast_conversion_succeeds() or a CoerceViaIO-only subset first, and add the DEFAULT syntax after the nested-cast rules are agreed?
Should a missing schema or relation in a reg* cast fall back to DEFAULT or raise an error?

committability.owner_note: Peter Eisentraut committed the prerequisite patches and removed himself as committer on 2026-04-10. The owner needs to know the parser, constant folding, expression execution and JIT.
committability.liability: Permanent standard syntax whose nested-cast and folding behaviour becomes a compatibility promise, a pg_proc column and CREATE FUNCTION option carried by pg_dump for good, and new executor and JIT steps.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v35, keeps the patch rebased, and moved the entry to PG20-3 himself on 2026-09-02.

priority.reason: ETL users and users of standard SQL gain, and the prerequisites are committed. The main patch is about 160 KiB across parser, planner, executor and JIT, and the nested-cast rule and the ERROR SAFE marker are not yet agreed.

provisional_note: Without the code, the cost of the new function-call steps and of soft-error constant folding for plain queries could not be judged. The two LLM-generated WIP patches in v35 could not be assessed either.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Precision loss casting float to numeric
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Robert Haas, Bear Giles
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make the float4 and float8 to numeric casts keep full binary precision, so that the cast and the round trip back to float no longer lose bits. The proof-of-concept patch printed values with FLT_DECIMAL_DIG and DBL_DECIMAL_DIG digits in place of FLT_DIG and DBL_DIG, and the author planned a frexp-based conversion.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane and Robert Haas expected more complaints about results such as 1.1::float8 casting to an odd-looking numeric than benefit from exact values, and Bear Giles asked that existing results not change. Making the cast follow extra_float_digits would make it stable instead of immutable. Per-schema casts cannot work because casts have no names, which left a separate named function as the remaining option. The author marked the entry Returned with feedback, citing the backward-compatibility issues and lack of time in this CF.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think there's probably a bigger chance of complaints that "casting 1.1::float8 to numeric now produces some weird, incorrectly-rounded result" than that we make anyone happier.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add internal Numeric to Uint64 conversion function.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Move the numeric-to-uint64 conversion code out of numeric_pg_lsn into a separate internal function. Other SQL functions that accept values up to the uint64 range could then call it.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The new function had no callers besides numeric_pg_lsn, so Tom Lane asked for a wider refactoring that also covers int64, and maybe float8, with existing callers of numeric_int8 moved to it. An API written without real callers gives no evidence that it handles cases such as errors in a useful way. No updated patch followed, so Robert Haas marked the entry Returned with Feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I'm way more interested in cleaning up the code
we have than in making things prettier for hypothetical future
call sites.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add Roman numeral conversion to to_number
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds Roman numeral input to to_number() with the 'RN' and 'rn' format masks, through a new roman_to_int() function in formatting.c. The function accepts mixed case and rejects non-canonical numerals under strict conversion rules.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane found that the patch bypasses NUM_processor with an if/else test, so literal text in the format fails and formats such as 'RN 999' are not rejected on input. He also asked for simpler error reporting that shows the whole input string, and he questioned rejecting non-canonical input. The author did not reply within 10 days, so Michael Paquier returned the patch with feedback. Robert Haas had earlier doubted that the feature was worth the added code.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think you need to be calling roman_to_int from the NUM_RN/NUM_rn
switch cases in NUM_processor, not trying to bypass NUM_processor
entirely.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add internal Numeric to Uint64 conversion function.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Move the numeric-to-uint64 conversion code out of numeric_pg_lsn into a separate internal function that other SQL functions can use. Later versions grew into a patch set that adds internal numeric conversion helpers and removes DirectFunctionCall() uses across numeric, pg_lsn, money and float8 code.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned the purpose of the patch set, because the author showed no clear performance gain and the refactoring added lines of code. The patch then stopped applying, and the author sent no update after May 2022, so the entry was closed as returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's apparently not for performance, and in terms of refactoring
you end up with more lines of code than before, so that doesn't seem too
appealing either.

precedents_retrieved.title: Implement NULL-related checks in object address functions to prevent cache lookup errors
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes the SQL functions pg_describe_object, pg_identify_object and pg_identify_object_as_address return NULL for undefined objects instead of raising "cache lookup failed" errors. It adds missing_ok flags to getObjectDescription, getObjectIdentity and lower-level lookup routines such as get_attname, GetForeignServer and the publication and subscription lookups.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Several preparatory patches were committed during the thread, but the main objectaddress patch was not. In its last review, Alvaro Herrera found that pg_identify_object returned an empty type in only some cases, and that it reported a column for a relation with no such column. The author fixed the column case, but left open whether type, operator and function formatting should be reworked to return NULL for undefined objects. The visible messages show no reply after that, and no closing message.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: One thing is that I am not sure if it is worth complicating the existing interface even more just to deal with undefined objects as pure NULLs.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add missing type conversion functions for PL/Python
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add direct conversion functions in PL/Python from Python objects to Postgres integer and float types, so values no longer go through the string-based PLyObject_ToDatum path. The author reported returned float8 arrays about 10 times faster.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Heikki Linnakangas found that the new tests showed changed behavior: on unpatched master, returning 100::float8 from a function declared to return int2 fails with "invalid input syntax for integer", but with the patch it succeeds. He said such behavior changes are not wanted, and the author agreed. No revised patch followed, and Michael Paquier returned the entry citing the behavior changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
So this patch is making some subtle changes to behavior. I don't think
we want that.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.
Reverted commit(s): Add error-throwing wrappers for the printf family of functions.; Permit use of vsprintf() in PostgreSQL code.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 16304a013432931e61e623c8d85e9fe24709d9ba, except
for its changes in src/port/snprintf.c; as well as commit
cac18a76bb6b08f1ecc2a85e46c9d2ab82dd9d23 which is no longer needed.

Fujii Masao reported that the previous commit caused failures in psql on
OS X, since if one exits the pager program early while viewing a query
result, psql sees an EPIPE error from fprintf --- and the wrapper function
thought that was reason to panic.  (It's a bit surprising that the same
does not happen on Linux.)  Further discussion among the security list
concluded that the risk of other such failures was far too great, and
that the one-size-fits-all approach to error handling embodied in the
previous patch is unlikely to be workable.

This leaves us again exposed to the possibility of the type of failure
envisioned in CVE-2015-3166.  However, that failure mode is strictly
hypothetical at this point: there is no concrete reason to believe that
an attacker could trigger information disclosure through the supposed
mechanism.  In the first place, the attack surface is fairly limited,
since so much of what the backend does with format strings goes through
stringinfo.c or psprintf(), and those already had adequate defenses.
In the second place, even granting that an unprivileged attacker could
control the occurrence of ENOMEM with some precision, it's a stretch to
believe that he could induce it just where the target buffer contains some
valuable information.  So we concluded that the risk of non-hypothetical
problems induced by the patch greatly outweighs the security risks.
We will therefore revert, and instead undertake closer analysis to
identify specific calls that may need hardening, rather than attempt a
universal solution.

We have kept the portion of the previous patch that improved snprintf.c's
handling of errors when it calls the platform's sprintf().  That seems to
be an unalloyed improvement.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support ORDER BY in CREATE FUNCTION for Set Returning Functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ORDER BY clause to CREATE FUNCTION so that a set-returning function can declare the order of its output, stored in pg_proc, letting the planner skip sorts that the declared order already satisfies. A new OrderCheck executor node verifies the declared order at runtime and raises an error if rows arrive out of order.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the patch adds substantial complication for users and developers to solve a narrow performance problem, and suggested instead teaching the planner to inline SQL functions with ORDER BY so double sorts are avoided transparently. Others discussed the cost of the runtime check and whether inlining covers non-SQL functions, without resolution. The last visible message (March 2015) notes it was unclear whether the patch was still being proposed and that it needed a rebase; no author response is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
TBH, my first reaction to this entire patch is unfavorable: it's a
solution in search of a problem.  It adds substantial complication not
only for users but for PG developers in order to solve a rather narrow
performance issue.

precedents_retrieved.title: psql: default to ON_ERROR_STOP
precedents_retrieved.summary: Make ON_ERROR_STOP on the default in psql, so a script or a series of -c and -f options stops at the first error and psql returns a nonzero exit status. The regression tests, which exercise failure cases, would run with ON_ERROR_STOP=0.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that the change would break far more existing scripts than it would help, because users who want this behavior already set it, and the default is about twenty years too late to change. He compared it to "set -e" in shell scripts, which is also not the default, and suggested documentation changes. Julien Rouhaud returned the entry because no documentation patch followed in the next few weeks.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The number of scripts you will break is far greater
than the number whose behavior will be improved, because people who
wanted this behavior will already be selecting it.

roaster_notes.note: No listed precedent matches; [P7] concerns object-address functions and its recorded reason does not apply. The relevant earlier rejections are inside this thread (messages #9 and #70).
Three objections are raised. The pg_dump changes for proerrorsafe follow the existing practice for function attributes, so they are not raised here.

Apart from the new pg_proc column, the feature adds no on-disk, WAL or wire-protocol state. Stored views go through ruleutils deparse, so pg_upgrade does not depend on the new node layout. Internal API changes such as evaluate_expr and ParseState affect only major releases.

No security objection found. Marking ERROR SAFE grants no new capability: C functions already need superuser, SQL and PL/pgSQL functions ignore the context, and a function that is wrongly marked still raises its errors as usual. For reg* casts, catalog existence is already visible, and message #90 shows the schema USAGE check stays a hard error. Not checked without the code: whether any soft path in the reg* lookups could also turn a permission or lock error into a fallback to DEFAULT.
Objections listed; none rest on precedents, since [P7] concerns object address functions and its recorded reason does not apply here.
The standard syntax and the function-based casts are not covered by any existing feature I can name, so this angle raises only the convenience question.

Demand for the core syntax looks real: the syntax is accepted into the SQL standard, Oracle has the same clause and SQL Server has TRY_CAST. Several independent reviewers also want it, so the remaining question is only how much surface beyond the text-ETL case is justified.
